cleanIntro: This guide comes from Browning's own owner's manual for the T-Bolt, the straight-pull rimfire rifle in .22 LR, .22 WMR and .17 HMR. The bolt is cycled by pulling it straight back and pushing it straight forward, with no lift, and it feeds from the Double Helix rotary magazine under the action. The field strip is two things out of the rifle: the magazine and the bolt, which comes out the back of the receiver past a small bolt release. Browning's book stops there, says not to take the rifle or the magazine any further apart, and says not to dry fire the T-Bolt.

steps.title: Safety on: slide it back until the red dot is covered
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and keep your fingers away from the trigger. The safety is the slide on the top rear of the receiver. Push it rearward with your thumb until the red warning dot is covered; with the dot showing, the rifle can fire. Leave it on safe for the whole strip, because Browning wants it on safe before the bolt goes in or comes out.
steps.quote: To move the “safety” to the on safe position slide the “safety” rearward with your thumb so that the red warning dot is covered
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Operation of the "Safety"
steps.warn: DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED COLOR ALONE TO INDICATE YOUR FIREARM’S SAFETY STATUS.

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Find the magazine release button underneath the rifle, just in front of the magazine. Press it with the index finger of your free hand and catch the magazine as it drops out. Do this before you touch the bolt, so working the bolt cannot feed another cartridge into the chamber. The rifle can still fire a chambered round with the magazine out.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button rearward and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Unloading > UNLOADING THE RIFLE, step 2
steps.warn: REMOVING THE MAGAZINE FROM THE RIFLE DOES NOT PREVENT THE RIFLE FROM BEING FIRED.

steps.title: Pull the bolt straight back and look in the chamber
steps.action: Pull the bolt handle straight back to the open position. That extracts and ejects any cartridge in the chamber. Then look into the chamber yourself to be sure it is empty, and leave the bolt open while you check. A rimfire case is small and easy to miss, so look rather than trust the ejection.
steps.quote: Draw the bolt to its rear or open position. This will extract and eject any live cartridge that may be in the chamber.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Unloading > UNLOADING THE RIFLE, step 3

steps.title: Empty the magazine and check everything is clear
steps.action: To empty the magazine, tip its front end down and turn the gear on its right rear side a little with your thumb. That takes off the spring pressure so the cartridges come out easily. Then check the chamber, the barrel and the magazine once more, and put all the ammunition away from where you will clean.
steps.quote: Rotate the gear slightly with your thumb. This releases spring pressure, allowing the cartridges in the magazine to be easily removed from the magazine.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Unloading > UNLOADING THE MAGAZINE, step 2
steps.warn: ALWAYS INSPECT THE CHAMBER, BARREL, AND MAGAZINE CAREFULLY AFTER UNLOADING TO BE SURE ALL LIVE CARTRIDGES ARE CLEARED FROM THE FIREARM.

steps.title: Close the bolt, then draw it back just a little
steps.action: With the chamber empty and the safety still on, push the bolt fully closed. Now pull the bolt handle back only slightly, just far enough to unlock the handle. Stop there: the bolt has to stay far enough forward that you can reach the bolt release. Pulled all the way back, you have gone past it.
steps.quote: With the bolt in the closed position, grasp the bolt handle and draw the bolt rearward slightly, just far enough to unlock the bolt handle, but far enough forward to allow access to the bolt release.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Inserting and Removing the Bolt > Removing the Bolt, step 2
steps.warn: BEFORE INSERTING OR REMOVING THE BOLT, ENSURE THE "SAFETY" IS IN THE ON SAFE POSITION.

steps.title: Press the bolt release until it clicks, bolt out the back
steps.action: Press the bolt release down with your finger until you feel it click. Keep it pressed and pull the bolt handle straight back, and the whole bolt slides out of the rear of the receiver. Put on eye protection for the cleaning that follows, as Browning asks for disassembly and cleaning.
steps.quote: Press the bolt release down with your finger until it clicks and pull the bolt handle rearward, removing the bolt from the rear of the receiver
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Inserting and Removing the Bolt > Removing the Bolt, step 3

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench now: the rifle with its stock and barrel, the bolt, and the empty magazine. That is the whole field strip for the T-Bolt. Browning's cleaning starts from exactly here, with the magazine and bolt out, so the bore can be cleaned from the action end. The book takes the rifle no further apart than this.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and bolt as explained previously.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 1

steps.title: Rod and patch in from the action end
steps.action: Use a cleaning rod with a slotted tip or a jag, and a patch big enough to fit the bore snugly. With the bolt out, put the rod in at the action end and run it back and forth several times. Do not let the rod hit the crown of the muzzle: damage there can spoil the rifle's accuracy.
steps.quote: Insert the rod and patch into the barrel at the action end and run it back and forth several times.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 2

steps.title: Heavy fouling: brass brush, pushed all the way through
steps.action: Some powder residue is normal and usually comes out with a patch soaked in nitro solvent. If the fouling is heavy, wet a brass bore brush with nitro solvent and scrub the chamber and bore until it is gone. Push the brush all the way out of the barrel before you pull it back, so the bristles do not break off.
steps.quote: To prevent brass bristles from breaking off, the brush should be pushed completely through the barrel before being withdrawn.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 3

steps.title: Dry the bore, then one slightly oiled patch
steps.action: When the fouling is out, wipe the chamber and bore dry. Then push one slightly oiled patch through to protect the bore, using a fine, light gun oil. Look through the barrel and into the chamber afterward to make sure no patch has been left behind.
steps.quote: When the bore is dry, pass a slightly oiled patch through it for preservation.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, steps 4-5

steps.title: Brush out the receiver, a light film of oil on moving parts
steps.action: Use a small brush or a rag to get dirt and debris out of the receiver and the other parts of the action, the bolt included. Then lightly oil the moving parts with a good light gun oil; a very thin film is enough. Do not pour oil in: it can drain down into the wood, soften it and loosen the stock for good.
steps.quote: Use a small brush or rag to remove dirt or other foreign matter from inside the receiver and other parts of the action.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 6
steps.warn: DO NOT POUR LARGE QUANTITIES OF OIL INTO THE RECEIVER OR OTHER PARTS.

steps.title: Do not take the rifle any further apart
steps.action: The bolt and the action are not taken apart any further. Browning calls the rifle a specialized, finely fitted mechanism that can be permanently damaged by trying to take the inner assemblies apart. If it needs more than this for service or cleaning, Browning sends you to a qualified gunsmith or its service facility in Arnold, Missouri.
steps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions

steps.title: Magazine stays together; leave the rear screw alone
steps.action: The Double Helix magazine is cleaned whole. Browning does not recommend taking it apart, and the assembly screw on the back of the magazine must not be touched: tampering with it will make the magazine stop working. Check the magazine often, because oil and dirt slowly build up inside the gear mechanism.
steps.quote: It is not recommended that the Double Helix™ magazine be disassembled.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING THE MAGAZINE
steps.warn: DO NOT TAMPER WITH THE ASSEMBLY SCREW ON THE REAR OF THE MAGAZINE.

steps.title: Fill with plastic-safe solvent, shake, drain, dry
steps.action: Spray the magazine inside and out with a gun cleaning solvent that is safe for its polymer body and will not corrode the metal parts. Fill the body with that solvent, cover the loading port with a finger, and shake it hard with the port pointed away from you. Drain out the solvent and the dirt, then dry it with compressed air or let it air dry.
steps.quote: Place your finger over the loading port and shake it vigorously (with the loading port away from you) to loosen residue in the magazine.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, steps 1-4

steps.title: Oiled cloth on the metal, oil or wax on the wood
steps.action: Wipe all the exposed metal with a lightly oiled cloth, getting every finger mark, because moisture collects in them. Give the metal a light film of oil whenever the rifle has been out in weather or handled a lot. Wood can be wiped with a light gun oil or polished with a good furniture wax, but use one or the other, not both.
steps.quote: Wipe all exposed metal surfaces with a lightly oiled cloth making certain that all finger marks are removed.
steps.cite: Browning T-Bolt Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (document code 25-BFA-088 on the closing lines) — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES, steps 7-8

deepAbsentReason: Browning's T-Bolt book ends at the field strip, with the magazine and bolt out, and forbids going further: under Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions it says "NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL." and sends any further disassembly to a qualified gunsmith or its Arnold, Missouri service facility. It also says the Double Helix magazine should not be disassembled. There is no deeper procedure to follow.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bolt out, and the rod goes in from the action end
A patch big enough to fit snugly, run back and forth several times
Do not let the rod strike the crown of the muzzle
Normal residue: a patch soaked in nitro solvent
Heavy fouling: brass brush with nitro solvent, pushed all the way through before it comes back
Chamber and bore wiped dry, then one slightly oiled patch
Check that no patch is left in the barrel or chamber

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & BOLT
tasks: Dirt out of the receiver and the action with a small brush or rag
Moving parts lightly oiled; a very light film is enough
Do not pour oil into the receiver; it drains into the wood
Never take the rifle apart further than the bolt and magazine

cleaning.name: DOUBLE HELIX MAGAZINE
tasks: Do not take the magazine apart
Do not tamper with the assembly screw on the rear of the magazine
Plastic-safe solvent inside and out, filled, shaken with the port away from you
Drained, then dried with compressed air or left to air dry

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & WOOD
tasks: All exposed metal wiped with a lightly oiled cloth, finger marks included
Wood: light gun oil or furniture wax, not both
Keep solvents, insect repellent and sunscreen off the finishes

reassembly: Make sure the chamber and magazine are empty and the safety is on, with the red dot covered.
Check the bolt handle is in the unlocked position. If it is not, hold the bolt with your left hand and pull the bolt handle rearward with your right hand; the bolt locks to the rear.
Line up the front end of the bolt with the opening at the back of the receiver and push the bolt all the way forward until it locks in place.
Push the empty magazine into the magazine well until the magazine latch holds it.
fncheck: With the rifle empty and pointed somewhere safe, pull the bolt straight back and push it fully forward, and feel it move smoothly and lock closed. Look at the top of the bolt: the red cocking indicator shows when the rifle is cocked. Slide the safety rearward until the red dot is covered, then forward until it shows, and feel it move positively both ways; leave it on safe. Do not pull the trigger to test anything: Browning says not to dry fire the T-Bolt, because it can damage the parts. Press the magazine release and check the magazine drops free, then push it back in until the latch holds it. Never test the rifle's function with live ammunition.
